title: Iran Releases First Video of Supreme Leader Khamenei Amid Growing Doubts Over His Health
excerpt: A 13-second clip purportedly shows Mojtaba Khamenei teaching religious studies, but questions about its authenticity underscore deepening uncertainty over who is actually governing Iran.
body:
• Iranian media released a 13-second video purportedly showing Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei teaching religious studies — his first appearance on video since taking office in March 2026.
  • The footage has raised questions about its authenticity, as Iranian media did not specify when or where it was recorded, fueling speculation it may have been filmed earlier.
  • Experts say rival political factions are increasingly invoking Khamenei's authority to attack each other, with one analyst stating he may be dead or "kept alive in an extremely unstable and severely deteriorated condition."
  • Khamenei suffered severe facial and leg injuries in the February 28 airstrike that killed his father, and has communicated only through written statements since his March 8 appointment.

Iranian state media have released a 13-second video clip purportedly showing Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei teaching religious studies to a group of students, marking what would be his first appearance on video since succeeding his father more than five months ago.

The footage, which surfaced this week, has immediately drawn scrutiny. Iranian media did not specify when or where the video was recorded, prompting speculation that it may have been filmed before the U.S.-Israeli airstrike that killed Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on February 28 and severely wounded his son.

A Leader Unseen Since Taking Power

Mojtaba Khamenei, 56, was appointed Iran's third supreme leader by a clerical assembly on March 8, days after the strike on the supreme leader's compound in central Tehran. He suffered a fractured foot and severe facial lacerations in the attack, according to three people close to his inner circle who spoke to Reuters.

https://x.com/htTweets/status/2086374956427010092

Since then, he has not appeared in public, delivered a speech, or granted an interview. His only communications have been written statements disseminated through a Telegram channel operated by his office. No audio or video recording had accompanied any of those statements until now.

"There's only so many times you can use someone's name without any proof of life that they actually exist. The longer Mojtaba is absent, the more questions develop over whether he is alive or able."

— Kasra Aarabi, Director of IRGC Research, United Against Nuclear Iran

Power Struggle Intensifies Behind Closed Doors

The video's release comes amid escalating infighting among Iran's political factions. Fox News reported that rival groups are increasingly invoking Khamenei's authority to undermine each other, even as doubts grow over whether he is actively governing.

In one episode reported by Iran International, senior cleric Mohammad-Bagher Kharrazi — a relative of the Khamenei family by marriage — claimed President Masoud Pezeshkian had repeatedly threatened to resign, and quoted the supreme leader as warning: "If he resigns one more time, I will approve it." Pezeshkian's office called the account "baseless and an outright lie."

A separate report alleged Pezeshkian met Khamenei only once, inside a vehicle with tinted windows at an undisclosed Tehran location. The encounter lasted several minutes, the two men could not see each other, and Pezeshkian was reportedly not permitted to shake Khamenei's hand. The president later questioned whether the voice he heard actually belonged to the supreme leader, according to the report.

Experts Divided on Whether Khamenei Can Govern

Kasra Aarabi, director of IRGC research at United Against Nuclear Iran, described the competing claims as reflecting a deeper struggle within what he called an "Islamist oligarchic mafia system" where the supreme leader functions as the "godfather" arbitrating among factions.

"Mojtaba's name is the glue that's holding the system together right now," Aarabi told Fox News. "Each of these clans invokes his name to justify its existence, legitimize its position, and consolidate its place within this fragile system."

Exiled Iranian journalist Mehdi Ghadimi went further, saying he did not believe there was "a functioning person by that name who is capable of thinking, making decisions or speaking." He added: "Either he is dead, or he is being kept alive in an extremely unstable and severely deteriorated condition."

The IRGC's Growing Dominance

Mojtaba Khamenei owes his elevation to Iran's Revolutionary Guards, who backed him as a reliable guardian of their hardline agenda. Already strengthened by the war, the Guards' growing dominance signals a more aggressive foreign policy and tighter domestic repression, according to Reuters.

Iranian President Pezeshkian said in July that his level of "interaction" with the supreme leader was "increasing day by day." But senior sources told Reuters that the absence of any image or voice recording was due to both health and security considerations, given the assassination of his father.

What to Watch

The authenticity and timing of the newly released video will likely face intense scrutiny from analysts and intelligence agencies. If the footage is confirmed as recent, it would represent the first tangible evidence that Khamenei is alive and functional since the February airstrike. If it proves to be archival, it could deepen the crisis of legitimacy already threatening Iran's theocratic system.

For Iran's regional posture and its ongoing negotiations with Washington, the question of who is actually making decisions in Tehran remains one of the most consequential unknowns in global geopolitics.
